chunks: From him, from al-Hasan, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the slaughtered meat of the People of the Book and their women, so he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of the People of the Book permissible for Muslims to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via Safwan al-Jammal affirms the permissibility of consuming the meat of the People of the Book and marrying their chaste women. It serves as a foundational textual proof for the Shia position that the Ahl al-Kitāb’s slaughter is valid, reinforcing the Quranic allowance in Surah al-Ma'idah while clarifying the practical application of this ruling in daily life.
